text_en: No evil will befall the one who fears the Lord, but in trials such a one will be rescued again and again.
text_cn: 敬畏上主的，决不会遭遇凶恶；受诱惑时，上主必一再保全他，由凶恶中拯救他。

text_en: The wise will not hate the law, but the one who is hypocritical about it is like a boat in a storm.
text_cn: 明智人不憎恶法律和正义；佯守法律的人，却像一只在波涛中飘荡的船。

text_en: The sensible person will trust in the law; for such a one the law is as dependable as a divine oracle.
text_cn: 聪明人信赖天主的法律，法律也忠于他，犹如乌陵的神谕。

text_en: Prepare what to say, and then you will be listened to; draw upon your training, and give your answer.
text_cn: 解答问题时，先要准备应说的话；如此，人才听你；先将教训综合起来，然后才可作答。

text_en: The heart of a fool is like a cart wheel, and his thoughts like a turning axle.
text_cn: 愚人的心，好像车轮；他的思念，好似旋转的轮轴。

text_en: A mocking friend is like a stallion that neighs no matter who the rider is.
text_cn: 好嘲弄人的朋友，就如见了牝（pìn）马的牡（mǔ）马，任何人骑它，它总是嘶鸣不已。

text_en: Why is one day more important than another, when all the daylight in the year is from the sun?
text_cn: 为什么这一天胜过那一天，虽然一年内，每天的光明，都是来自太阳？

text_en: By the Lord’s wisdom they were distinguished, and he appointed the different seasons and festivals.
text_cn: 太阳造成以后，循规蹈矩，因上主的智慧，日子才有了区别。

text_en: Some days he exalted and hallowed, and some he made ordinary days.
text_cn: 他规定了不同的时令和季节，以便在那些时节内，依时庆祝一些节日：

text_en: All human beings come from the ground, and humankind was created out of the dust.
text_cn: 他将一些日子，提高列为圣日；将其余的日子，则列为平日。众人都是从土来的，因为，亚当就是用土造成的。

text_en: In the fullness of his knowledge the Lord distinguished them and appointed their different ways.
text_cn: 上主以自己的绝大智慧，使众人各有分别，使他们的道路各有不同。

text_en: Some he blessed and exalted, and some he made holy and brought near to himself; but some he cursed and brought low, and turned them out of their place.
text_cn: 他们中有被他祝福而抬举的，有被他祝圣，然后引他们亲近自己的；但也有被他诅咒和贬抑，从本位上被推翻的。

text_en: Like clay in the hand of the potter, to be molded as he pleases, so all are in the hand of their Maker, to be given whatever he decides.
text_cn: 有如泥土在陶工手里，可以任意捏造处置；

text_en: Good is the opposite of evil, and life the opposite of death; so the sinner is the opposite of the godly.
text_cn: 要做什么样式，都系于陶工的意思；同样，人在创造者手里，上主照自己的决定，来处理他们。

text_en: Look at all the works of the Most High; they come in pairs, one the opposite of the other.
text_cn: 善与恶相对，生与死相峙，罪人也与虔敬人敌对：请看至高者的一切化工：无不两两相对，一一对立。

text_en: Now I was the last to keep vigil; I was like a gleaner following the grape-pickers;
text_cn: 最后我也醒悟了，来搜集箴言，如同在收获葡萄的人后面，拾取残余的人；

text_en: by the blessing of the Lord I arrived first, and like a grape-picker I filled my wine press.
text_cn: 蒙上主的祝福，我预先着手工作，也像收获葡萄的人一样，填满了我的榨酒池。

text_en: Consider that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek instruction.
text_cn: 请注意！我不是单为我自己劳苦，也是为一切寻求教导的人。

text_en: Hear me, you who are great among the people, and you leaders of the congregation, pay heed!
text_cn: 你们为民众官长的，请听我的话；你们为集会首领的，请侧耳静听。

text_en: To son or wife, to brother or friend, do not give power over yourself, as long as you live; and do not give your property to another, in case you change your mind and must ask for it.
text_cn: 几时你还在世上，不要将你的权柄，交给儿子、妻子、兄弟和朋友，也不要将你的产业，交与别人，怕你将来后悔，而有求于他们。

text_en: While you are still alive and have breath in you, do not let anyone take your place.
text_cn: 当你还活着，气息尚存的时候，不要让任何人支配你。

text_en: For it is better that your children should ask from you than that you should look to the hand of your children.
text_cn: 你的子女有求于你，胜于你望着你子女的手。

text_en: Excel in all that you do; bring no stain upon your honor.
text_cn: 在你所行的一切事上，你应作主。

text_en: At the time when you end the days of your life, in the hour of death, distribute your inheritance.
text_cn: 不要污辱你的荣誉。在你寿命结束之日，在你快要去世之时，应分清你的遗产：

text_en: Fodder and a stick and burdens for a donkey; bread and discipline and work for a slave.
text_cn: 草料、棍杖、驮重，是属于驴的；面包、训戒、劳作，是属于仆人的。

text_en: Set your slave to work, and you will find rest; leave his hands idle, and he will seek liberty.
text_cn: 你要吩咐他工作，这样你就可以放心；若你放任他，他就要找寻自由自在。

text_en: Yoke and thong will bow the neck, and for a wicked slave there are racks and tortures.
text_cn: 轭（è）与皮鞭，可以屈服强硬的颈项；不断的工作，可以使仆人柔顺。

text_en: Put him to work, in order that he may not be idle,
text_cn: 对待恶仆只有鞭打和刑罚；要使他们操作，不得空闲，

text_en: for idleness teaches much evil.
text_cn: 因为，空闲教给人许多坏事。

text_en: Set him to work, as is fitting for him, and if he does not obey, make his fetters heavy. Do not be overbearing toward anyone, and do nothing unjust.
text_cn: 要给他指定与他相宜的工作；若他不服从，就叫他带脚镣；但对于任何人不要过分。未审度以先，什么重大的事也不要做。

text_en: If you have but one slave, treat him like yourself, because you have bought him with blood. If you have but one slave, treat him like a brother, for you will need him as you need your life.
text_cn: 你若有一个忠信的仆人，对待他要如同对待你自己一样，因为他是你用血汗换来的；要待他如同兄弟，因为你需要他，正如需要你自己一样。

text_en: If you ill-treat him, and he leaves you and runs away,
text_cn: 若你待他不好，他必要逃跑；

text_en: which way will you go to seek him?
text_cn: 若他傲然离去，你向谁去追问；你不知道，你在哪条路上去寻找他。
